notes: Always convert percent to decimal before using in formula.
Match the rate and base: Base corresponds to 100%.
formulaCard.title: Portion Formula

explanation: The [[kw:portion formula]] is used to solve percent problems: [[imp:$\text{Portion} = \text{Rate} \times \text{Base}$]].
[[kw:Base]] (B): the whole or original amount (the "of" number).
[[kw:Rate]] (R): the percent written as a decimal or fraction (usually with % sign).
[[kw:Portion]] (P): the part or amount that the percent represents.
Identify which part is unknown and solve: P = R × B, R = P ÷ B, B = P ÷ R.

visuals.title: Portion Formula Components
visuals.caption: Portion = Rate × Base. Identify two knowns to find the third.

teacherCues: Write: Portion = Rate × Base on the board.
Explain each component with a real-world example.

steps: Use formula: P = R × B → P = 0.3 × 200 = 60.

examples.title: B – Explain the base
steps: The base is the whole amount that the percent refers to.
It's the starting point; 100% corresponds to the base.
The portion is the part that matches the given rate.

blocks.title: 1. The Portion Formula: Base, Rate, Portion

discoveryHook.scenario: You buy a $25 shirt at a 20% discount. How much do you save? The original price is the base, the percent is the rate, and the savings is the portion. The formula is: Portion = Rate × Base.

challengeCorner.prompt: A store marks up a $120 item by 45%. What is the selling price? (Hint: find markup portion, then add to base).

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: Don't confuse the portion with the base. [[imp:The base is the whole; the portion is a part.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: You saved $15 on a $75 item. What percent discount did you get? Rate = 15 ÷ 75 = 0.20 = 20%. The rate tells you the percentage relationship.

examples.prompt: A basketball player makes 18 out of 24 free throws. What is his free throw percentage?
examples.title: A – Find percent from numbers

examples.prompt: If the rate is 0.25, what does that mean in words?
examples.title: B – What does the rate tell us?
steps: It means 25 out of every 100, or one-quarter of the base.
So the portion is one-fourth of the base.

examples.title: C – Find the discount rate
examples.prompt: A $200 item is on sale for $150. What is the discount rate?

questions.prompt: To find the rate, divide the ___ by the base.
A student answered 35 out of 50 questions correctly. What percent is that?
If you saved $12 on a $80 item, what percent discount is that?

confusionCorner.body: The portion must be the same 'kind' as the base. [[imp:If base is original price, portion is discount or sale price, not both.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

challengeCorner.prompt: A class has 40 students; 28 passed the exam. What percent failed? (Hint: first find the number who failed.)

visuals.caption: Rate = Portion ÷ Base. Divide, then convert to percent.
visuals.title: Finding the Rate

notes: R is a decimal; multiply by 100 to get percent.
formulaCard.title: Rate Formula

explanation: When the portion and base are known, the rate is found by [[imp:$R = \frac{P}{B}$]].
The result is a decimal; multiply by 100 and add % to express as a percent.
Use when you know the part and the whole, and need the percentage.
Example: 12 out of 60 students are absent → $12 \div 60 = 0.20 = 20\%$ absent.

blocks.title: 2. Solving for the Rate (Percent)
teacherCues: Show that the answer will be a decimal; convert to percent.

challengeCorner.prompt: After a 20% increase, a salary is $48,000. What was the original salary? (Hint: 120% of original = 48,000)

confusionCorner.body: Don't add or subtract the portion to find the base. [[imp:Use division: B = P ÷ R.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

questions.prompt: To find the base when you know portion and rate, ___ the portion by the rate.
A 5% commission earned you $250. What was the total sales amount?

examples.prompt: You paid $18 in tax, which is 6% of the purchase price. What is the purchase price?
examples.title: A – Find original price

steps: P = R × B, so B = P ÷ R.
Since the portion is a fraction of the base, you reverse the multiplication to find the whole.
Multiplying would give a portion of the portion, not the base.
examples.title: B – Why divide?
examples.prompt: If you know 25% of a number is 30, why do you divide 30 by 0.25 instead of multiplying?
examples.peerPrompt: Think about the portion formula: P = R × B.

examples.prompt: A 30% discount on a jacket saved you $21. What was the original price?
examples.title: C – Find base from a discount

discoveryHook.scenario: A 20% discount saved you $10. To find the original price (base), you divide: Base = 10 ÷ 0.20 = $50. The base is the unknown whole that the percent is taken from.

blocks.title: 3. Solving for the Base (Whole Amount)

notes: Base is always larger than the portion unless rate > 100%.
formulaCard.title: Base Formula

explanation: When the portion and rate are known, the base is found by [[imp:$B = \frac{P}{R}$]].
Use when you know a part and its corresponding percent, and you need the original whole.
Remember: the rate must be written as a decimal before dividing.
Example: 40% of a number is 30 → $B = 30 \div 0.40 = 75$.

visuals.caption: Base = Portion ÷ Rate. Answer is the whole amount.
visuals.title: Finding the Base

teacherCues: Show the formula: Base = Portion ÷ Rate.
Use real-world examples like '20% off saved me $10, what was the original price?'
Show formula: Percent Change = (Amount of Change ÷ Original) × 100.
Give examples of sales tax, discounts, pay raises.
blocks.title: 4. Percent Increase and Decrease

challengeCorner.prompt: A shirt originally $45 is on sale for $36. What percent discount is applied?

confusionCorner.body: If the percent change is negative, it's a decrease. [[imp:Use the original value as the base, not the new value.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

questions.prompt: To calculate percent change, divide the amount of change by the ___ amount.
A salary rose from $50,000 to $55,000. What is the percent increase?
A stock fell from $80 to $60. What is the percent decrease?

examples.title: A – Price increase
examples.prompt: A movie ticket went from $12 to $15. Find the percent increase.

examples.peerPrompt: Think about what 'change compared to what?' means.
examples.prompt: In a price drop from $50 to $40, why is 50 the base and not 40?
examples.title: B – Why original as base?
steps: Percent change always compares the change to the starting (original) point.
Using $40 as base would give a different (and incorrect) percentage.
The phrase 'from X to Y' tells you that X is the original.

examples.prompt: A town's population dropped from 15,000 to 12,000. Find the percent decrease.
examples.title: C – Population decrease

formulaCard.title: Percent Change Formula
notes: Base is always the original amount.

explanation: [[kw:Percent Change]] measures how much a value has gone up or down relative to the original.
Formula: [[imp:$\text{Percent Change} = \frac{\text{Amount of Change}}{\text{Original Amount}} \times 100$]]
If the new amount is greater than the original, it's a percent increase.
If the new amount is less, it's a percent decrease.
Be careful: the base for percent change is always the original amount, not the new amount.

discoveryHook.scenario: Gas price rose from $3.00 to $3.60. The increase is $0.60. To find the percent increase: $0.60 ÷ 3.00 = 0.20 = 20%. This formula works for any increase or decrease.

teacherCues: Use the blueprint: Understand → Translate (identify P, R, B) → Solve → Conclude.
Work through mixed-up problems to decide which element is unknown.

discoveryHook.scenario: A restaurant bill is $80, and you want to leave a 20% tip. Tip = 0.20 × $80 = $16. When the bill already includes a 15% service charge, the calculations involve identifying what is the base.

questions.prompt: In a percent problem, the whole amount is the ___.
A $250 camera is on sale for 30% off. How much is the sale price?
A bill total is $108, including 8% tax. What was the price before tax?

blocks.title: 5. Solving Percent Word Problems

visuals.title: Word Problem Blueprint
visuals.caption: Identify P, R, B correctly; the rest is arithmetic.
headers: Example (Original price before 20% discount that saved $10)

rows.1: Does it make sense? Check discount.

explanation: Percent word problems often require identifying the base, rate, and portion from the story.
Use the blueprint: 1. Understand: what is given? 2. Translate into the P/R/B elements. 3. Solve with the appropriate formula. 4. Conclude: check the answer’s reasonableness.
Common pitfalls: confusing the base with the new amount after a change, or forgetting to convert percent to decimal.
Practice with a mix: find portion (e.g., tax, tip, discount), find rate (e.g., grade percentage), find base (e.g., original price before tax).

formulaCard.title: Checklist for Percent Problems
formulaCard.formula:
Ask: What is the whole? (Base)
What percent? (Rate)
What is the part? (Portion)
Then use the formula for the unknown.

hints: 20% increase then 20% decrease is not the original because the base changes.
